maria: Quick signal — saw a p99 spike on the streaming-chat route during a mixed workload run. putting it here before i lose context.

kevin: Can you drop the p95/p99 numbers and which kernels/models were in play?

maria: p95 ~180ms, p99 ~420ms baseline (chat streaming tiny-mb=2, kernel=fast-attn-v1). Under mixed load with non-streaming completions (mb=16, kernel=matmul-v2) p99 jumps to ~560ms. KV cache miss rate up ~3x in the same window. snippet from trace:```
[2026-03-14T21:03:12Z] request 0xabc kernel-switch start
[2026-03-14T21:03:12Z] request 0xabc kv_eviction=true
[2026-03-14T21:03:12Z] kernel-switch end (+128ms)
[2026-03-14T21:03:12Z] kv-reshard start
[2026-03-14T21:03:13Z] kv-reshard end (+210ms)
```

jen: Hmm — sounds like the kernel selection path is not sticky per-request, so when a completion batch comes in it flips the backend for that worker and forces KV reshuffle/eviction. That explains the additional copy/reshard cost.

kevin: We measured kernel-switch overhead: median ~120ms, tail adds ~200ms when cache needs reshuffle. Repro command I used: `./perf_run --mix 70:30 --mb-chat 2 --mb-comp 16 --trace kernel-switch` — reproduces the jump reliably on a 4-GPU canary.

maria: Proposal: implement per-route microbatch policy + "sticky kernel" pinning for streaming chat requests: once a request starts on kernel A, keep all subsequent chunks for that request on A until completion. Add hysteresis (500ms) to avoid toggling for short-lived bursts. Also add async KV prewarm on kernel change (spawn a low-priority prewarm that copies hot KV segments). Thoughts? :thinking_face:

jen: +1. For safety, expose a runtime flag and do A/B with 5% traffic. We'll need metrics: per-request kernel-switch count, kv-eviction rate, p95/p99. :thumbsup:

perf-bot: Perf snapshot (local preflight): baseline mixed p99=560ms -> sticky-kernel p99=330ms -> sticky+kvcache-prewarm p99=290ms. CPU overhead ~+2%. Logs note `kv_prewarm_ok` on 87% of switches.

kevin: Nice numbers. Next steps: the feature flag rollout (5% -> 25% -> 100%) and trace capture on canary fleet. Also add a watch to abort if p99 regresses >10% vs baseline for 30m. i'll open a PR for the sticky-kernel runtime flag and a small prewarm worker.

maria: I'll attach the profiling artifacts and sample traces to the PR. Thanks all — pushing to canary tonight.
